subject: math.AT
name: Freyd’s generating hypothesis
statement: Must a map between finite spectra that induces zero on every stable homotopy group be null-homotopic?
importance: It asks whether homotopy groups faithfully detect maps in the finite stable homotopy category.
status_note: Analogues in other triangulated categories have different answers; the original finite-spectra problem is unresolved.

references.title: Large self-injective rings and the generating hypothesis

subject: math.AT
name: Weak chromatic splitting conjecture
statement: For every prime p and height n at least one, does the canonical map L_(n−1)S_p to L_(n−1)L_K(n)S_p admit a retraction, where L_(n−1) is E(n−1)-localization and L_K(n) is Morava K(n)-localization?
importance: It describes how successive chromatic layers of the stable homotopy category fit together.
status_note: This is the weak splitting assertion; stronger explicit decompositions have counterexamples, and the telescope conjecture is false.

references.title: A short introduction to the telescope and chromatic splitting conjectures

subject: math.AT
name: Moore’s rational-ellipticity exponent conjecture
statement: For a simply connected finite CW complex X with finite-dimensional rational homotopy, does each prime p admit an exponent e such that p^e annihilates all p-primary torsion in π_*(X)?
importance: It would relate rational homotopy complexity to uniform bounds on integral torsion.
status_note: The implication stated here is the rationally elliptic direction; exponent results for spheres and selected spaces do not establish the general case.

subject: math.AT
name: Hilali conjecture
statement: For a simply connected rationally elliptic finite CW complex X, is the total dimension of π_*(X) tensor Q at most the total dimension of H^*(X; Q)?
importance: It proposes a basic quantitative link between rational homotopy and cohomology.
status_note: Rationally elliptic means both total rational homotopy and total rational cohomology are finite-dimensional; many restricted classes are known.

references.title: Hilali conjecture and complex algebraic varieties

subject: math.AT
name: Halperin’s fibration conjecture
statement: If F is a simply connected rationally elliptic finite CW complex with positive Euler characteristic, must the rational Serre spectral sequence of every fibration F → E → B with simply connected base collapse at E_2?
importance: It would rigidly control the cohomology of fibrations with positively elliptic fibers.
status_note: The positive Euler characteristic and rational ellipticity hypotheses are essential; the general case remains open.

references.title: Halperin’s conjecture in formal dimensions up to 20

subject: math.AT
name: Toral rank conjecture
statement: If the r-dimensional torus acts almost freely on a finite CW complex X, must the sum of the rational Betti numbers of X be at least 2^r?
importance: It connects the size of a continuous symmetry group to the minimum topology of the space it acts on.
status_note: Almost free means all stabilizers are finite; numerous special cases are proved but the general topological assertion is open.

references.title: The Toral Rank Conjecture and variants of equivariant formality

subject: math.AT
name: Carlsson’s free-action rank conjecture
statement: If (Z/pZ)^r acts freely and cellularly on a finite CW complex X, must the sum of the dimensions of H^i(X; F_p) be at least 2^r?
importance: It is a central obstruction to free finite-group actions on small complexes.
status_note: This is the topological free-action conjecture; counterexamples to some purely algebraic rank analogues do not resolve this formulation.

subject: math.AT
name: Whitehead’s asphericity conjecture
statement: Is every connected subcomplex of an aspherical two-dimensional CW complex itself aspherical?
importance: It would strongly constrain how higher homotopy can arise inside low-dimensional complexes.
status_note: Aspherical means all homotopy groups in degrees at least two vanish; special classes of two-complexes are understood.

subject: math.AT
name: Novikov conjecture
statement: Are the rational higher signatures of every closed oriented smooth manifold invariant under orientation-preserving homotopy equivalences, when defined using its classifying map to the classifying space of its fundamental group?
importance: It connects characteristic classes, manifold topology, and large-scale properties of groups.
status_note: The conjecture is known for many classes of groups, but remains unresolved for arbitrary fundamental groups.

subject: math.AT
name: Curtis conjecture
statement: Is the positive-degree image of the mod-2 stable Hurewicz homomorphism π_*^s to H_*(Q_0S^0; F_2) generated only by the images of Hopf-invariant-one and Kervaire-invariant-one elements?
importance: It predicts exactly which stable homotopy classes can be detected in the homology of the infinite loop space of the sphere.
status_note: The existence problem for the dimension-126 Kervaire class has been resolved; that result does not settle this Hurewicz-image conjecture.

references.title: The weak conjecture on spherical classes
